types.embedding_query_text: MonetaryValue: A quantity of money, often expressed with a currency. Also called AmountOfMoney, CurrencyValue, FinancialAmount, Price. Examples: 140 million euros, $161m.

candidates.comment: A general group of related items, which may or may not be of the same kind, forming a sequence or collection. Also called collection, sequence, set, installment. Examples: a book series, a lecture series, a product line, a collection of artworks. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is a series of creative works.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: FootballManager: A person responsible for managing a football team. Also called SoccerManager, Coach, HeadCoach, TeamManager. Examples: Jose Mourinho, Alvaro Arbeloa, Portuguese veteran Jose Mourinho.

chosen_type.label: FootballManager
chosen_type.definition: A person responsible for the overall management and coaching of a football team.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically describes a person in the role of a football manager; the closest general type is Person.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: AutomatedTeller
candidates.comment: A FinancialService provided by a machine for banking transactions. Also called ATM, cash machine, automated banking machine. Examples: "Bank of America ATM", "Wells Fargo cash machine", "independent ATM kiosk".

candidates.label: BusOrCoach
candidates.comment: A BusOrCoach is a Vehicle designed to carry multiple passengers, with coaches being luxury versions for long-distance travel. Also called omnibus, motorcoach, passenger bus, tour bus. Examples: city bus, Greyhound coach, school bus, double-decker bus.

candidates.label: AutoRental
candidates.comment: An AutoRental is an AutomotiveBusiness that provides vehicles for temporary hire. Also called car hire, vehicle rental agency, rent-a-car. Examples: Hertz, Enterprise Rent-A-Car, a local van rental service. Distinct from AutoDealer, which sells vehicles.

types.embedding_query_text: Role: The function assumed or part played by a person or thing in a particular situation. Also called Position, Capacity, Function, Duty. Examples: coach.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Role' is an exact match for schema.org's Role, which describes a function or position.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

types.embedding_query_text: Trophy: A cup or other decorative object awarded as a prize for a victory or success. Also called Award, Prize, Championship, Medal. Examples: major trophy.

chosen_type.label: Trophy
chosen_type.definition: A cup or other decorative object awarded as a prize for a victory or success.
chosen_type.justification: No specific schema.org class for a 'Trophy' as a physical object; 'Thing' is the most general appropriate parent.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: MediaOutlet: An organization that publishes or broadcasts news and information. Also called NewsSource, Publisher, Broadcaster, JournalismOutlet. Examples: Spanish media.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'MediaOutlet' is an exact match for schema.org's NewsMediaOrganization, which explicitly lists 'media outlet' as an alias.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: AdvertiserContentArticle
candidates.comment: An AdvertiserContentArticle is an Article that has been paid for or produced to the specifications of an external entity. Also called sponsored article, advertorial, native advertising, paid content. Examples: A blog post promoting a product written by an influencer, a sponsored news segment, an article funded by a brand. Distinct from NewsArticle, which is typically produced by independent journalists.

candidates.label: BroadcastEvent
candidates.comment: A BroadcastEvent is a PublicationEvent representing an event that is transmitted over the air or online. Also called live broadcast, streamed event, televised event, radio broadcast. Examples: a live news report, a sports game broadcast, a concert livestream.

candidates.label: MediaSubscription
candidates.comment: An intangible service that grants a user access to media content, including audio, video, or books. Also called content subscription, media access plan, digital media membership. Examples: a streaming video subscription, an audiobook service membership, a digital newspaper subscription.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

types.embedding_query_text: Concern: A matter of interest or importance to someone, or a feeling of worry. Also called Worry, Issue, Apprehension, Anxiety. Examples: concerns over the size of the transfer fee.

chosen_type.label: Concern
chosen_type.definition: A matter of interest or importance to someone.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class represents an abstract 'concern' or 'worry'; Intangible is a suitable parent for such a concept.

mentions: concerns over the size of the transfer fee

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: DeliveryChargeSpecification
candidates.comment: A price specification detailing the cost associated with delivering an offer using a particular method. Also called Shipping cost, delivery fee, freight charge, postage cost. Examples: "Standard shipping: $5.99", "Express delivery: $15.00", "Free delivery for orders over $50". Distinct from DeliveryMethod, which describes the method itself, not its cost.

candidates.label: UnitPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value detailing the price asked for a specific offer by an organization or person. Also called price details, cost specification, offer price. Examples: "$10.99 per item", "€50 per hour", "£2.50 per unit".
